canons.name: Catholic
canons.summary: Scripture for the Catholic Church since the Council of Trent (1546), which listed Tobit, Judith, Wisdom, Sirach, Baruch and 1–2 Maccabees among the Old Testament's books, and required Esther and Daniel 'entire with all their parts', the Greek additions included.

sources.title: Council of Trent, Session IV, Decree concerning the Canonical Scriptures (1546)
sources.author: tr. T. A. Buckley

canons.name: Eastern Orthodox
canons.summary: Read as part of the Old Testament, which the Orthodox Church receives in the Greek Septuagint. The Synod of Jerusalem (1672) named Wisdom, Judith, Tobit, Susanna, Bel and the Dragon, the Maccabees and Sirach as scripture; editions differ on 1 Esdras, 3 and 4 Maccabees, the Prayer of Manasseh and Psalm 151, and Slavonic Bibles add 2 Esdras.

sources.title: Confession of Dositheus (Synod of Jerusalem, 1672), Question 3
sources.author: tr. J. N. W. B. Robertson, ed. D. Bratcher

sources.title: What books are in the Orthodox Old Testament?
sources.author: St. Michael Antiochian Orthodox Church
sources.note: 'Some editions also include 3 Maccabees, 4 Maccabees, Psalm 151, 1 Esdras, and the Prayer of Manasseh'

sources.title: World English Bible, preface: 'Does the World English Bible include the Apocrypha?'
sources.note: the Slavonic Bible includes 2 Esdras as 3 Esdras

canons.name: Ethiopian Orthodox
canons.summary: The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church counts 81 books, among them Jubilees and Enoch, which survive whole only in Ge'ez, and the third and fourth Esdras. Its three books of Meqabyan are not 1–2 Maccabees, and lists of the 81 vary.

sources.title: The Bible
sources.author: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church
sources.note: the church's list of its 46 Old Testament and 35 New Testament books

canons.name: Anglican: read, not canon
canons.summary: The Church of England's Article VI lists these among the books the Church 'doth read for example of life and instruction of manners; but yet doth it not apply them to establish any doctrine'. The 1611 King James Bible printed them as their own section between Malachi and Matthew.

sources.title: The Holy Bible, conteyning the Old Testament and the New (London: Robert Barker, 1611)
sources.note: the Apocrypha printed between Malachi and Matthew
